question.text: A triangle has sides $x$, $y$, and $z.$ The sides $x$ and $z$ have lengths $3$ and $4$, respectively. If the angle $Y$ between $x$ and $z$ has a measure of $139^\circ$, what is the length of side $y ?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

The Law of Cosines states that \[ y^2 = x^2+z^2-2xz\cos{Y}, \] Here, we have \[ m\angle{Y} = 139^{\circ}, \quad x = 3, \quad z = 4. \]

Substituting the numbers into the formula gives \[ \begin{align} y^2 &= 3^2+4^2-2(3)(4)\cos{139^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 9+16-24\cos{139^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 25-24(-0.754\,70\ldots)\\[3pt] &= 25+18.113\,03\\[3pt] &= 43.113\,03 \end{align} \] rounded to $5$ decimal places.

Taking the square root gives \[ y = \sqrt{43.113\,03} = 6.57 \] rounded to two decimal places.

question.text: For the triangle above, find $m \angle M$ in degrees to two decimal places.
question.explanation: We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $M\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} \cos{M} &= \frac{n^2+l^2 - m^2}{2nl}.\\ \end{align} \] Here, we have \[ m=29,\quad n=20,\quad l=13. \] This gives \[ \begin{align} \cos{M} &= \dfrac{20^2+13^2 - 29^2}{2(20)(13)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{400+169- 841}{520}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-272}{520}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-34}{65}. \end{align} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{align} m\angle M &= \arccos\left(-\dfrac{34}{65}\right) \\[5pt] &=121.54^\circ. \end{align} \] rounded to two decimal places.

question.explanation:
The Law of Cosines states that \[ b^2 = a^2+c^2-2ac\cos{A}. \] Here, we have \[ m\angle{A} = 140^{\circ}, \quad a = 15, \quad c = 7. \] Substituting the numbers into the formula gives \[ \begin{align} b^2 &= 15^2+7^2-2(15)(7)\cos{140^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 225+49-210\cos{140^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 274-210(-0.766\,04\ldots)\\[3pt] &= 274 +160.869\,33\\[3pt] &= 434.869\,33 \end{align} \] rounded to $5$ decimal places.

Taking the square root gives \[ b = \sqrt{434.869\,33} \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 21} \] rounded to the nearest integer.

question.text: Rounded to the nearest tenth of a degree, $m\angle B\approx$
question.explanation: We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $B\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} \cos{B} &= \dfrac{a^2+c^2 - b^2}{2ac}.\\ \end{align} \] Here, we have \[ a=9,\quad b=6,\quad c=7. \] This gives \[ \begin{align} \cos{B} &= \dfrac{9^2+7^2 - 6^2}{2(9)(7)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{81+49- 36}{126}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{94}{126} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{47}{63}. \end{align} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{align} m\angle B &= \arccos\left(\frac{47}{63}\right)\\[5pt] &\approx\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{41.8}^\circ \end{align} \] rounded to the nearest tenth.

example.title: Calculating the Measure of an Angle in a Triangle Using the Law of Cosines

question.text: A triangle has sides $x$, $y$, and $z.$ The sides $x$, $y$, and $z$ are of lengths $8$, $15$, and $17$, respectively. In degrees, what is the measure of the angle $X$ between the sides $y$ and $z ?$ Round your answer to the nearest tenth of a degree.
question.explanation:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} \cos{X} &= \dfrac{y^2 + z^2 - x^2}{2yz}. \end{align} \]

Here, we have \[ x = 8, \quad y = 15, \quad z = 17. \]

This gives \[ \begin{align} \cos{X} &= \dfrac{15^2 + 17^2 - 8^2}{2(15)(17)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{225 + 289 - 64}{510}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{450}{510} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{15}{17}. \end{align} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{align} m\angle X &= \arccos\left(\frac{15}{17}\right)\\[5pt] &\approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{28.1}^\circ \end{align} \] rounded to the nearest tenth.
